messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Quarterly SLA playbook & KPI pass-off — latency, spend, uptime

Team — attaching the working Q2 KPI pack (Q2_KPI_Pack_v3.pdf) and a raw latency dump (latency-dash-raw.csv). This is the internal pass-off ahead of the May 28 QBR readout. Please review and flag anything that cannot land as-is under leadership review.

Top asks (please respond inline):
- Latency: confirm we can commit to the 99th pct SLO slide (slide 7). If your data disagrees, note corrections + owner.
- Cost: the projected model-spend reduction (~12%) is baked into slide 12 — need a line-item verification by model family.
- Uptime: include a brief incident wrap on slide 4 (owner + RCA link).
- Usage: call out the April mid-month dip (slide 9). Is that a reporting artifact or real?

Timeline: please return comments by end-of-day Friday (5/22). I will consolidate and produce the final deck Monday morning for exec distribution.

Attachments: Q2_KPI_Pack_v3.pdf (draft), latency-dash-raw.csv (export)

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly SLA playbook & KPI pass-off — latency, spend, uptime

Vanessa — quick pass. I dug into the cost numbers and have a few immediate concerns: the slide showing model family savings assumes a work mix shift to smaller-replica variants that we have not yet validated on production traffic. I'm attaching a short workbook (cost-breakdown-models.xlsx) with the per-model assumptions; please review.

Specific asks / notes:
- Cost: See tab 'assumptions' — we should not commit to the 12% reduction without a validated run of the new batching profile. Markus: can you confirm the runtime perf delta by EOD Thursday?
- Latency: Slide 7 conflates 95th and 99th windows when the long-tail requests (seq>2k) dominate the 99th; suggest adding a footnote or separate long-tail slide.
- Usage dip (slide 9): this looks like a reporting window mismatch between the analytics pipeline and billing timestamps — Irene, can you cross-check the ingestion-time vs billed-time windows?

Attachment: cost-breakdown-models.xlsx (workbook)

- Laura
VP, Product Operations
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly SLA playbook & KPI pass-off — latency, spend, uptime

Laura / team — I ran the microbench and a small production shadow run to validate the batching/quantization changes. Short summary:
- Expected median latency improvement for the target models: 6–8% under the new kernel. 99th pct for long-tail (seq>2k) improved ~3% in shadow, not enough to change the 99th SLO on slide 7.
- The 12% cost reduction is achievable on synthetic mixes; on current real traffic the estimate drops to ~7%. I'm attaching a short analysis (latency-tail-analysis.pdf).

Proposed mitigation: add a fallback policy to route >2k seq requests to a higher-capacity instance class to protect the 99th while we tune batching. That would add modest spend but keep SLOs intact.

Irene: I'll hand you the perf logs and the shadow-run trace (link in the Drive doc) so you can fold the numbers into the uptime/incident narrative.

Attachments: latency-tail-analysis.pdf

- Markus
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Consolidated Q2 KPI Pack + next steps

Thanks all — consolidation complete. Summary and explicit owners below (final deck attached: Q2_KPI_Pack_v3_final.pdf). I will hold off external distribution until we have written sign-off from owners.

Decisions / clarifications:
- Latency SLO: keep the published 99th SLO on slide 7; add a separate 'Long-tail handling' slide with the fallback policy Markus proposed. Owner: Markus — deliver fallback policy text by Mon 5/25.
- Cost: update conservative estimate to 7% for exec narrative and include Laura's workbook as an appendix. Owner: Laura — confirm appendix wording by Mon 5/25.
- Uptime / incidents: Irene to produce a one-paragraph RCA summary and link to the incident timeline (include planned maintenance notes). Owner: Irene — due Tue 5/26.
- Usage dip: Irene to reconcile ingestion vs billing timestamps and confirm whether the April dip is an artifact. Owner: Irene — due Tue 5/26.

External share plan: after internal sign-off (target Tue 5/26 EOD), I will send a tailored packet to Arcadia (contact: Emily Zhao) and loop Procurement if we need to document spend changes ahead of the renewal conversation.

Artifacts / links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Q2kpi-VANESSA-Q2, hubspot:deal:HB-47291
Attachments referenced: Q2_KPI_Pack_v3_final.pdf, latency-dash-raw.csv, cost-breakdown-models.xlsx, latency-tail-analysis.pdf
